newsitem.title: USA: CoreStates, Andersen in technology alliance.
newsitem.headline: CoreStates, Andersen in technology alliance.

text.p: CoreStates Financial Corp and Andersen Consulting Thursday announced an agreement in principle to establish a 10-year information technology alliance.

CoreStates will retain control over its technology strategy, direction, priorities and decision making, and Andersen Consulting will concentrate on developing industry-leading applications and delivering technology services in support of CoreStates' business goals. The companies said the value of the contract will be finalized in negotiations over the next few months.
CoreStates said it expects the alliance will have a "negligible impact" on 1997 earnings.

Andersen Consulting is expected to manage activities that represent approximately 40 percent of CoreStates' current overall technology operations. Most of the affected technology operations are housed Philadelphia, where CoreStates is headquartered. All of the approximately 300 CoreStates employees who will be affected by the alliance will be offered positions with either CoreStates or with Andersen Consulting.

Terrence Larsen, chairman and chief executive of CoreStates, said in a statement that the goal of the alliance was to raise capacity and produce consistent "world class" quality rather than to simply reduce costs.
Goals of the alliance include enhancing revenues by facilitating new product development and improvement in the return on technology investment, the companies said.
A spokesman for CoreStates said in response to a question that the bank has been working with Andersen Consulting for more than a year and the contract was not put out for a bid.
